designation: IN THE COURT OF DISTRICT & SESSIONS JUDGE
jurisdictionNote: District-level criminal and civil courts in Chhattisgarh, governed by the Madhya Pradesh Civil Courts Act, 1958 (as adopted by Chhattisgarh) and the Chhattisgarh High Court Rules. Sessions courts try offences punishable with imprisonment exceeding 7 years. Chhattisgarh, carved out of Madhya Pradesh in 2000, presently comprises 33 districts after the 2022 reorganisation. Hindi is the official language of the State subordinate courts under the Chhattisgarh Rajbhasha Adhiniyam, 2007.

party_designation.state: State of Chhattisgarh through the Principal Secretary, Home Department, Government of Chhattisgarh, Raipur

prayer_language.opening: It is, therefore, most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may graciously be pleased to:
prayer_language.closing: And for this act of kindness, the petitioner shall, as in duty bound, ever pray.

verification_format:
I, {deponent_name}, {designation}, do hereby solemnly verify and declare that the contents of the above petition from paragraph ___ to paragraph ___ are true to my personal knowledge and the contents of paragraphs ___ to ___ are believed to be true on the basis of information received and legal advice tendered, which I believe to be true. Nothing material has been concealed therefrom.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

DEPONENT
localRules: Hindi is the official language of the Chhattisgarh subordinate courts under the Chhattisgarh Rajbhasha Adhiniyam, 2007; pleadings in English are accepted but Hindi translation may be insisted upon.
Bail applications under S.483 BNSS must disclose any earlier rejection by the Magistrate or any co-ordinate court.
Anticipatory bail applications (S.482 BNSS) must be accompanied by an affidavit, certified copy of the FIR and grounds of apprehension.
Vakalatnama in the form prescribed under the Chhattisgarh High Court Rules to be filed at the first instance with the requisite court-fee stamp.
All civil pleadings to be paginated, indexed and accompanied by a list of documents under Order VII / Order VIII CPC.
Court-fee under the Chhattisgarh Court-Fees Act, 1870 (as adopted) read with State amendments.
Atrocities (SC/ST), POCSO and NDPS cases are tried by designated Special Courts notified by the State Government — typically the District & Sessions Judge at the district headquarters.
Designated Special Courts also exist for offences under the Chhattisgarh Vishesh Jan Suraksha Adhiniyam, 2005.

After the 2022 reorganisation, four new districts (Khairagarh-Chhuikhadan-Gandai, Manendragarh-Chirmiri-Bharatpur, Mohla-Manpur-Ambagarh Chowki, Sakti) were notified; jurisdictional headquarters follow Government of Chhattisgarh and High Court notifications.
e_filing_note: e-Filing is operational at Bilaspur, Raipur and Durg via the eCourts portal; not yet mandatory state-wide.
